title: Trapped Rainwater Volume
statement: You are given a list of non-negative integers heights, where each value is the height of a solid bar of width 1 standing in a row. After a rainstorm, water pools on top of the bars wherever there are taller bars on both sides. The water resting above position i rises to min(tallest bar at or left of i, tallest bar at or right of i), so the units of water held at i equal that minimum minus heights[i], and never less than zero. Return the total units of water trapped across the whole row as a single integer. If the list has fewer than 3 bars there is nowhere to hold water, so return 0.
hints: Water above each bar is capped by the shorter of the two walls surrounding it, so what two quantities do you need to know at every position at once?

Walk two pointers inward from both ends while tracking the running maximum seen from each side; the smaller running maximum is the binding wall, so it is safe to settle that side's water and step it inward.

Advance whichever pointer has the smaller running max: move it one step, and if the new bar exceeds that side's running max update the max, otherwise add (running max - new bar) to the total, since the taller opposite running max guarantees the water is held.
